drufiy.com.title: DrufiyAI | AI systems for difficult operations

lines: Most tools tell you something broke.

products.heading: Lear and Prash, built from the same belief.
products.intro: We choose a hard operational problem and stay with it until the work becomes simpler for the people doing it.

cards.name: Lear
cards.description: A local DevOps agent for small engineering teams. Lear reads your real infrastructure signals, finds what actually broke, and proposes a fix that waits for your approval.

cards.name: Prash
cards.description: Prash was our first model for CI and CD failures. It taught us how much context a narrow problem demands, and became the foundation for Lear.

howWeBuild.heading: We go deep before we go wide.
howWeBuild.sub: The work starts with a real pain point, not a broad category and a polished demo.

steps.title: Find the unresolved problem
steps.body: Talk to the people carrying the operational load and study the failure in context.

steps.title: Build a dedicated model
steps.body: Design the reasoning, data, and evaluations around one job.

steps.title: Test it in real systems
steps.body: Put it in front of the people who need it and learn from what happens.

whatWeBelieve.heading: Useful systems know their boundaries.
whatWeBelieve.sub: Trust is designed into the way our models observe, decide, and act.

principles.title: Asks before it acts
principles.body: People stay in control of consequential changes.

principles.title: Proves every fix
principles.body: A suggestion is not a solution until the system confirms it.

principles.title: Runs close to the work
principles.body: Local operation keeps sensitive context where it belongs.

principles.title: Knows where it stops
principles.body: When the evidence is incomplete, the model says so.

leadForm.heading: Working on a problem generic AI keeps missing?
leadForm.sub: Tell us what the system is doing, what you have tried, and where the usual tools stop helping.

hero.eyebrow: Autonomous on-call · runs on your infra
hero.h1: The AI on-call engineer for teams too small to have one.
hero.body: Lear watches your CI, cloud, and Kubernetes from inside your own infrastructure. When something breaks, it finds the cause and writes the fix in plain English. Nothing touches production until you approve.

screenshot.alt: The Lear desktop app: a mission-control dashboard showing 86% infrastructure health, 10 of 13 connectors active, and live telemetry across AWS, GCP, and Kubernetes.

loopTeaser.heading: One agent. It watches, reasons, asks, then fixes.

steps.title: Watches
steps.body: your CI, cloud, and Kubernetes, with full context.

steps.title: Diagnoses
steps.body: finds the actual root cause, not a guess.

steps.title: Proposes
steps.body: one clear fix, explained in plain English.

steps.title: You approve
steps.body: nothing touches production without your yes.

steps.title: Fixes & verifies
steps.body: runs the fix and confirms the system recovered.

liveDemo.heading: A real recovery, start to finish.
liveDemo.disclosure: Lear has diagnosed and fixed real failures on real AWS and GCP machines, after approval. The full recording is on its way.

screenshot.alt: Lear Copilot answering 'check what happened to AWS' with a live status report for the ap-south-1 region, including a real EC2 node inventory pulled from the account.

onYourInfra.heading: It runs on your infrastructure. Not ours.
onYourInfra.body: Connect any of thirteen integrations with your own credentials. Lear checks them against the real provider APIs and works where your systems already live. Your credentials never leave your environment. Every action is proposed, approved, and written to a log the agent cannot edit.

screenshot.alt: Lear's Connect Your Infrastructure screen: configuring live credentials for one of thirteen backend services, grouped by infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, security, and infrastructure-as-code.

positioning.heading: Everyone else built this for enterprises. We built it for you.

savingsTeaser.heading: Find out what firefighting is costing your team.

pricing.heading: You only pay a slice of what we save you.
pricing.body: Start with a free, read-only trial. When you are ready, Lear earns the right to act. Pricing is 15 to 20% of the savings we measure together. If we do not save you money, you do not pay us.

closingCta.heading: See what Lear could save your team.

/how-it-works.h1: One agent. It watches, reasons, asks, then fixes.

steps.title: Read
steps.body: Lear watches CI, cloud, and Kubernetes with full context: logs, recent changes, config, and events.

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.body: It works out the real root cause, using a diagnosis engine tested against real production failures.

steps.title: Propose
steps.body: It writes one fix and explains it, in plain English, over Slack or email.

steps.title: Approve
steps.body: You say yes. By default, nothing runs without a human. Approval is the whole point.

steps.title: Execute
steps.body: It runs the fix on your infrastructure, using credentials that never leave your environment.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: It checks the system actually recovered, and logs everything.

honestLimits.heading: What Lear will not do on its own.
honestLimits.body: Lear will not autonomously change production databases or customer data, and will not reroute production networking or load balancers. Those stay with your engineers.

/trust.h1: Lear runs on your infrastructure, not ours.

pillars.title: Your infra, your credentials
pillars.body: Lear runs inside your own environment. Credentials never leave it, and no hosted third party ever touches them.

pillars.title: Approval by default
pillars.body: Five permission modes, and the default is "ask." Nothing runs in production without a human yes.

pillars.title: A log the agent can't edit
pillars.body: Every proposed and executed action is written to an append-only audit trail. The agent cannot rewrite its own history.

pillars.title: Dry-run anything
pillars.body: See exactly what Lear would do before it does anything real.

pillars.title: A circuit breaker
pillars.body: If something loops or starts to look wrong, Lear stops itself before you have to.

/trust.deliberateLimits: No autonomous changes to production databases or customer data. No production network or load-balancer changes. Those stay human, on purpose.

/savings.h1: See what Lear saves your team.
/savings.pricingNote: Lear costs 15-20% of what it saves you. You keep the rest.
/savings.disclosure: These are your numbers, not our customer results. We're pre-launch and showing the math in the open so you can check it. The model counts only recovered engineer time, conservatively, and ignores avoided downtime revenue.

/contact.body: Want to see Lear running on your own infrastructure, or just have a question? Book a 30-minute call with a founder, or email us directly.

threeAgents.title: Failure Diagnosis
threeAgents.body: Analyzes CI logs and pinpoints root causes automatically within seconds of a failure.

threeAgents.title: Automated Fixes

threeAgents.title: PR Verification

howItWorks.heading: From failure to fix in four steps

steps.title: Connect your repo
steps.body: Install via GitHub App in 30 seconds. Works with any existing workflow.

steps.title: Detect & diagnose
steps.body: Prash watches your GitHub Actions and analyzes failures instantly as they happen.

steps.title: Fix & create PR
steps.body: Automatic fixes are generated, tested, and a PR is opened and ready for review.

steps.title: Verify & ship
steps.body: All CI tests pass before Prash marks the fix verified. No false positives.

stats.note: Root cause in seconds, not hours of manual log trawling.

stats.label: Automated fixes that work
stats.note: Verified through your full CI pipeline before opening the PR.

stats.label: Zero config overhead
stats.note: Install the GitHub App. Prash figures everything else out.
